ai.literal: Graciousness called exceedingly great beauty, by its existence, exists this world.
ai.translation: This world continues to exist because of the presence of that exceedingly great beauty called graciousness.
ai.modern: கண்ணோட்டம் என்று சொல்லப்படும் மிகச் சிறந்த அழகு இருப்பதால்தான் இந்த உலகம் நிலைபெற்று இருக்கிறது.
ai.explanation: The couplet declares that the world continues to exist only because of human compassion or graciousness. It describes this quality as an 'exceedingly great beauty' (கழிபெருங் காரிகை), elevating it above mere physical attractiveness. Without this fundamental empathy connecting people, human society and the world as we know it would cease to function.

ai.literal: In consideration exists world-nature; that without-they existence to earth burden.
ai.translation: The proper functioning of the world rests on gracious consideration. The existence of those who lack it is merely a burden to the earth.
ai.modern: உலகத்தின் இயக்கம் இரக்கம் என்னும் பண்பில்தான் நிலைபெற்றுள்ளது. அந்தப் பண்பு இல்லாதவர்கள் உயிரோடு இருப்பது பூமிக்குப் பாரமே ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: The couplet explains that the world functions smoothly because people show consideration and grace to one another. The word 'கண்ணோட்டம்' refers to this kind look or compassionate consideration. If people lack this quality, their mere existence ('உண்மை') serves no purpose and only adds physical weight ('பொறை') to the earth.

ai.literal: Melody what becomes, to song harmony if not? Eye what becomes, graciousness without eye?
ai.translation: What is the use of a melody if it does not harmonize with the song? What is the use of eyes if they lack graciousness?
ai.modern: பாடலோடு பொருத்தம் இல்லை என்றால் பண்ணால் என்ன பயன்? அதுபோலவே, இரக்க குணம் இல்லை என்றால் கண்ணால் என்ன பயன்?
ai.explanation: This couplet uses a musical analogy to explain the true purpose of eyes. A melody ("பண்") is useless if it does not harmonize ("இயைபு") with the song it accompanies. In the exact same way, the physical eyes ("கண்") serve no real purpose if they lack a gracious, compassionate look ("கண்ணோட்டம்"). The repetition of "என்னாம்" (what is the use) emphasizes that just as music needs harmony, human sight requires empathy to be meaningful.

ai.literal: Existing like in the face what will do by the measure kindliness lacking eye
ai.translation: What good are eyes that merely seem to exist on the face, if they lack the proper measure of kindliness?
ai.modern: முகத்தில் இருப்பது போலத் தோன்றும் கண்கள், தகுந்த கண்ணோட்டம் இல்லாவிட்டால் என்ன பயனைத் தரும்?
ai.explanation: The couplet questions the very purpose of eyes if they do not express compassion. Eyes that lack kindliness are described as merely appearing to exist on the face. Without the essential quality of empathy, they are reduced to mere physical features that serve no true human purpose.

ai.literal: To the eye, ornament is graciousness; that if without, sore as to be perceived it will be.
ai.translation: Graciousness is the true ornament for the eyes. Without it, they will be considered mere sores.
ai.modern: கண்களுக்கு உண்மையான அணிகலன் இரக்கமாகும். அந்த இரக்கம் இல்லாவிட்டால், கண்கள் முகத்தில் உள்ள வெறும் புண்கள் என்றே கருதப்படும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the true purpose and beauty of the eyes. The word 'kaṇṇōṭṭam' literally means the flowing of the eyes, which signifies a gracious, compassionate look towards others. The poet states that this graciousness is the only real ornament ('aṇikalam') for the eyes. If the eyes lack this quality, they are not truly eyes but will be perceived merely as sores ('puṇ') on the face. The contrast between a beautiful jewel and a painful sore emphasizes that physical eyes are worthless without inner kindness.

ai.literal: With earth joined, tree-like they are; with eyes having joined, eyes-not-running they.
ai.translation: Those who have eyes but do not look with graciousness are merely like trees rooted in the earth.
ai.modern: கண்கள் இருந்தும் பிறரிடம் இரக்கம் காட்டாதவர்கள், மண்ணில் நிலைத்து நிற்கும் மரங்களுக்கு ஒப்பானவர்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet plays on the literal meaning of the Tamil word for graciousness, which implies the 'running' or extending of the eyes towards others. The poet states that people who possess physical eyes but fail to look upon others with empathy are no different from trees. Even though they exist in human form, their lack of compassion makes them as unfeeling and stationary as a tree rooted in the dirt.

ai.literal: Graciousness those-who-lack eyes they-lack; eyes those-who-possess graciousness even-the-lack is-not.
ai.translation: Those who lack graciousness do not truly have eyes. For those who truly possess eyes, there is no lack of graciousness.
ai.modern: கண்ணோட்டம் இல்லாதவர்கள் கண்களை உடையவர்கள் அல்லர். உண்மையான கண்களை உடையவர்களிடம் கண்ணோட்டம் இல்லாமல் இருப்பதில்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet equates the physical possession of eyes with the moral quality of graciousness or compassionate consideration (கண்ணோட்டம்). The poet states that people who lack this graciousness are effectively blind, as their eyes do not serve their true human purpose. Conversely, those who truly possess eyes will never be found lacking in graciousness. The repetition of the word 'கண்' (eye) emphasizes that true vision is not merely physical sight, but the ability to look upon others with kindness.

ai.literal: Duty without spoiling to show consideration to those who are able, right possesses this world.
ai.translation: This world rightfully belongs to those who are able to show consideration without compromising their duty.
ai.modern: தம்முடைய கடமை கெடாமல் மற்றவர்களிடம் இரக்கம் காட்ட முடிகிறவர்களுக்கு, இந்த உலகம் உரிமை உடையதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explores the delicate balance between executing one's responsibilities and maintaining human empathy. The phrase 'கருமம் சிதையாமல்' stresses that a person's primary duty or task must never be compromised. At the same time, 'கண்ணோட வல்லார்க்கு' highlights the rare ability to still show consideration and grace to others. The text concludes that the world rightfully belongs to those who can successfully harmonize strict duty with compassionate understanding.

ai.translation: Showing consideration and enduring the actions of even those whose nature is to cause harm is the foremost virtue.
ai.modern: பிறருக்குத் துன்பம் செய்யும் குணம் உடையவர்களிடத்தும் இரக்கம் காட்டி, அவர்கள் செய்யும் குற்றத்தைப் பொறுத்துக்கொள்ளும் குணமே மிகச் சிறந்ததாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the highest form of graciousness or consideration. It states that one should show consideration even to those who actively cause harm. The phrase 'பொறுத்து ஆற்றும் பண்பே தலை' emphasizes that bearing with such people and continuing to act with a forgiving nature is the foremost quality. The word 'கண்ணோடி' literally means the eyes running towards someone, which signifies looking upon them with kindness and empathy regardless of their hostile nature.

ai.literal: Being poured even having seen, poison having consumed they will be calm, esteem-worthy graciousness those who desire.
ai.translation: Those who desire highly esteemed graciousness will calmly drink poison, even when they see it being poured for them.
ai.modern: எல்லாராலும் விரும்பத்தக்க சிறந்த நாகரிகத்தை விரும்புபவர்கள், தமக்கு நஞ்சை ஊற்றுவதைப் பார்த்தாலும், அதனை உண்டு அமைதியாக இருப்பார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet illustrates the extreme extent of graciousness and benignity. It says that those who value noble, esteemed social conduct will accept even poison from others without causing a scene. By drinking the poison calmly, they prioritize the feelings and dignity of the person serving it over their own lives. The word 'நாகரிகம்' (urbanity or graciousness) here denotes a profound, self-sacrificing courtesy that refuses to embarrass another person.
